softwareSystems.name: SeeForce
softwareSystems.description: Turns C4 annotations embedded in a codebase's own source files into an interactive architecture diagram. Used to answer "what does this codebase actually do, and how do its pieces talk to each other?"
softwareSystems.short_desc: Turns C4 annotations in your code into an interactive architecture diagram

containers.name: Frontend
containers.description: Display architecture data as a comprehensive graph; handles auth-gated routing
containers.short_desc: Renders the architecture graph and handles auth-gated routing

relationships.description: Fetches graph data and manages user session (auth)

components.name: Lexicon
components.description: Provides per-project glossary to the graph — loads terms via SWR, distributes them through React context, highlights matching terms in blue within node descriptions and edge relationship labels, and shows the definition in a slide-up bottom panel on click.
components.short_desc: Per-project glossary — highlights and defines terms in the graph

relationships.description: fetches and mutates lexicon entries
injects lexicon context into the ReactFlow node tree

components.name: Auth Context
components.description: React context that manages authentication state; checks session on load and exposes logout
components.short_desc: React auth state — checks session on load, exposes logout

relationships.description: GET /api/auth/me/ to check session, POST /api/auth/logout/ to sign out

components.name: Overlay Editor
components.description: Sliding detail panel for the selected node or edge — shows name, description, tags, and source-file link; in edit mode, saves overlay edits and manages the lexicon terms relevant to the node's description (add, edit, delete).
components.short_desc: Sidebar panel to view and edit a node or edge's overlay details

relationships.description: reads the shared glossary via context to find terms relevant to the node being edited
saves node/edge overlay edits and lexicon entry changes

components.name: Architecture Visualizer
components.description: Display architecture and manage user interaction such as drilling down on specific component
components.short_desc: Renders the graph and handles drill-down between C1/C2/C3 views

relationships.description: Renders C4 element nodes in the ReactFlow canvas
Renders directional relationship edges between nodes
opens the detail/edit panel for the clicked node or edge

components.name: Node manager
components.description: Handles node management
components.short_desc: Renders System/Container/Component nodes on the graph canvas

relationships.description: highlights and links glossary terms found in node description

components.name: Edge manager
components.description: Renders directional relationship edges between nodes using floating edge geometry — connects to nearest border point of each node.
components.short_desc: Renders relationship edges between nodes with floating geometry

relationships.description: highlights and links glossary terms found in edge relationship labels

containers.name: Backend
containers.description: Serves the REST API for project CRUD, node/edge overlays, lexicon entries, sharing, and GitHub import/sync/link. Persists everything to the Database and delegates codebase parsing to Annotation Parser — it does not parse source files itself.
containers.short_desc: REST API for project CRUD, overlays, lexicon, and GitHub import/sync

relationships.description: Reads and writes architecture graph data via Django ORM
Delegates user authentication via GitHub OAuth 2.0 (django-allauth); also mints short-lived GitHub App installation tokens (JWT-signed) to fetch repo content for import/sync
parses and builds workspace.json when scanning a repo locally via manage.py scan

components.name: Graph transformer
components.description: Takes an already-built workspace.json (read from ProjectMap.source_json — never re-parses source files itself) and converts the requested C1/C2/C3 view into ReactFlow-ready nodes and edges, including placeholder nodes for out-of-view relationship targets.
components.short_desc: Converts workspace.json into ReactFlow nodes and edges per view

components.name: GitHub App Token Manager
components.description: Signs a JWT with the GitHub App's private key and exchanges it for a short-lived (1h) installation access token, used to authenticate GitHub API calls on behalf of one installation instead of a long-lived OAuth token.
components.short_desc: Mints short-lived GitHub App installation tokens for API calls

relationships.description: Signs the app JWT (RS256), reads an installation's owning account via /app/installations/{id}, and exchanges the JWT for a 1h installation access token via /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens

components.name: Local Scan Command
components.description: The manage.py scan command — scans one or more local repo paths and upserts the resulting ProjectMap. This is the direct-CLI ingestion path; it does not go through GitHub, so github_repo/github_branch are left unset.
components.short_desc: Scans local repo paths and upserts the resulting ProjectMap

relationships.description: parses annotation blocks from the target repo path(s)
resolves relationships and assembles the parsed elements into workspace.json
creates or updates the ProjectMap row for the scanned project

components.name: Auth API
components.description: Exposes /api/auth/me/ and /api/auth/logout/; delegates GitHub OAuth flow to django-allauth, reports whether the user has a GitHub App installation, and hands back the GitHub App's install/configure URL
components.short_desc: Session check, logout, and GitHub App install status/URL

relationships.description: OAuth 2.0 login and identity resolution
reads the user's GitHub SocialAccount and GitHubAppInstallation rows

components.name: GitHub App Setup Endpoint
components.description: Receives GitHub's post-install/post-update redirect, verifies with GitHub that the installation belongs to the logged-in user's own GitHub account, and links the installation_id to that SeeForce user.
components.short_desc: Handles GitHub's post-install redirect and links the installation

relationships.description: Reads the installation's owning GitHub account to verify the caller actually performed this installation
creates or updates the GitHubAppInstallation row for the logged-in user

components.name: Edit API
components.description: Handles all user-driven mutations on a project map — node description overlays, edge label overlays, and per-project lexicon entries (create, update, delete). Also serves project CRUD and the view endpoint that returns a rendered graph for a given level.
components.short_desc: User mutations — node/edge overlays, lexicon CRUD, project CRUD

relationships.description: reads and writes ProjectMap, NodeOverlay, EdgeOverlay, and LexiconEntry rows
converts the requested project's workspace.json into ReactFlow nodes/edges for the view endpoint

components.name: GitHub Import
components.description: Imports, re-syncs, and links project architecture to GitHub repositories. Repo access is scoped per user by matching the repo's owner login against their GitHub App installations (a user may have several — personal + org); GitHub App Token Manager mints an installation token for the matching install, falling back to their newest installation, then to an unauthenticated request for public repos with no install. Fetches .seeforce/workspace.json via the GitHub Contents API and upserts it as a ProjectMap. Blob links are built client-side from github_repo/github_branch, not here.
components.short_desc: Imports, re-syncs, and links project architecture from GitHub

relationships.description: Fetches .seeforce/workspace.json via GitHub Contents API, authenticated with an installation token when one covers the repo, unauthenticated otherwise
Requests a fresh installation token before each Contents API call
creates or updates the ProjectMap row for the imported, synced, or linked repo

containers.name: Annotation Parser
containers.description: Standalone library (published as seeforce-c4parser) that parses @c1/@c2/@c3/@lexicon annotations from a repo's source files and assembles the resulting workspace.json. Independently packaged and shared by the Backend and the SeeForce CLI, not owned by either.
containers.short_desc: Parses C4 annotations from source files into workspace.json

components.name: Annotation Scanner
components.description: Walks a repo's source files and parses @c1/@c2/@c3/@lexicon annotation blocks out of comments and docstrings into a flat list of elements. Does not resolve relationships or assemble workspace.json — that's Workspace Builder, which takes this list as its input.
components.short_desc: Walks source files and extracts @c1/@c2/@c3/@lexicon blocks

components.name: Workspace Builder
components.description: Takes the flat element list from Annotation Scanner, resolves every "uses:" reference into a concrete element id, and assembles the final workspace.json structure — systems, containers, components, relationships, and views. Also the structural drift gate — find_orphans and find_empty_containers catch level-mixing, ambiguous refs, orphan elements, and C2s with zero C3s before the workspace is written.
components.short_desc: Resolves relationships into workspace.json; the structural drift gate

components.name: Static Facts Extractor
components.description: Statically extracts imports, top-level definitions, and adjacent docstrings from source files (Python, TypeScript) as an unverified candidate signal — never a source of truth. Isolated in its own subpackage behind extract_facts() so tree-sitter (an optional dependency) can be dropped without breaking annotation scanning or building.

containers.name: SeeForce CLI
containers.description: Local command-line entry point — logs in, scans a repo for @c1/@c2/@c3/@lexicon annotations, launches an LLM-guided annotation pass, and installs the SeeForce MCP server plus the drift-sync tooling (Stop hook, skill, CLAUDE.md rule) that keeps a project's annotations from drifting from its code going forward.
containers.short_desc: CLI — login, scan, annotate, and installs the drift-sync tooling

relationships.description: parses and builds workspace.json when scanning a repo locally via `seeforce scan`
authenticates the user, fetches the project id, and registers the MCP server against it via `seeforce mcp install`

components.name: MCP Install Command
components.description: Registers the SeeForce MCP server in ~/.claude.json and writes the drift-sync tooling (arch-sync-check.sh Stop hook, seeforce-arch-check skill, CLAUDE.md rule section) into the target repo — the delivery mechanism that makes ongoing drift checking happen in a user's own project, not just a one-time annotate_codebase pass.
components.short_desc: Registers the MCP server and installs the drift-sync hook/skill

relationships.description: Fetches the project id and validates the auth token via `seeforce mcp install`

containers.name: MCP Server
containers.description: Exposes SeeForce architecture context to AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) via the Model Context Protocol over stdio — get_context, find_component, get_file_owner, get_architecture_for_files, and annotate_codebase let assistants query containers, components, and file ownership without reading source files. Ships as the seeforce-mcp entry point inside the seeforce-cli pip package.
containers.short_desc: Exposes SeeForce architecture context to AI coding assistants via MCP

relationships.description: Fetches workspace architecture data via REST API

components.name: Workspace Navigation Helpers
components.description: Pure lookup helpers over the fetched workspace dict — enumerating systems, containers, components, and external systems, and rendering a relationship as a human-readable line for tool output.

components.name: Static Facts Bridge
components.description: Collapses the file-level import graph from Static Facts Extractor into component-level candidate edges by resolving each endpoint through file ownership inference, dropping intra-component pairs so only cross-component candidates reach the LLM. Receives already-extracted facts as a parameter — it never calls the extractor itself.

relationships.description: resolves each edge endpoint's owning component

components.name: Ownership Inference
components.description: Infers which C4 component or container owns a given file path — via exact source_file match, same-directory proximity, or nearest-parent-directory fallback when nothing is annotated yet.

relationships.description: looks up known components and containers to match a file path against

components.name: Workspace API Client
components.description: Fetches the current project's workspace.json from the Backend over REST, resolving which project to fetch via a configured project UUID or falling back to the most recently updated one.

relationships.description: fetches workspace architecture data via REST API

components.name: Tool Handlers
components.description: Answers the 5 architecture questions an AI assistant can ask — get_context (system overview), find_component (search by keyword), get_file_owner (which component owns a file), get_architecture_for_files (drift check for edited files), and annotate_codebase (the C4 annotation guide plus source files, for a first-time annotation pass).
components.short_desc: Implements the 5 MCP tools assistants call to query architecture

relationships.description: Fetches workspace architecture data via REST API

components.name: Static Facts Query Handler
components.description: Implements the get_static_facts_for_files MCP tool — extracts import/definition facts for the requested files via Static Facts Extractor, then collapses them into component-level candidate edges via Static Facts Bridge, formatting both as tool output for the calling AI assistant.

relationships.description: extracts imports, definitions, and docstrings for the requested files
collapses extracted facts into component-level candidate edges via ownership inference

softwareSystems.name: GitHub
softwareSystems.description: Source of truth for project architecture (via .seeforce/workspace.json in repos) and OAuth 2.0 identity provider for SeeForce users; also target of source file links from the graph
softwareSystems.short_desc: Source of truth for architecture data and OAuth identity provider
